entities.summary: Tso Moriri or Lake Moriri, 4,522 m (14,836 ft), is a pristine high-altitude lake and a Ramsar Wetland Site in the remote Changthang Plateau in the Leh district of the union territory of Ladakh in India. As the largest high-altitude lake entirely within India and Ladakh's Trans-Himalayan region, it spans 26 km north-south and 3-5 km wide. The lake is fed by three primary glacial streams - Karzok Phu (west), Gyama Phu (north), and Phirse Phu (southwest) - which form extensive marshes at their deltas.
